answer: Agents can make high-value actions contingent on a vault-backed stake that is slashable when independent audits prove an identity farm is coordinating duplicate claims. The protocol links claims to costly, time-locked deposits, then randomly challenges a sample and rewards honest auditors from forfeited stake. A Sybil operator must lock real capital for every persona and risks losing it if caught; spreading identities no longer creates free voting weight. An ember or raven may be a harmless agent label, but neither bypasses the deposit or audit.
